summary: Howard Carter's team uncovered the first step leading down to the almost intact tomb of the pharaoh Tutankhamun in the Valley of the Kings.
reason: Carter, funded by Lord Carnarvon, had searched the valley for years for a tomb he believed was still undiscovered.
significance: It became the most famous archaeological find in history and sparked worldwide interest in ancient Egypt.
place: Valley of the Kings, Luxor, Egypt

title: The Soviet Union is founded
summary: Delegates from Russia, Ukraine, Belarus and the Transcaucasian republic approved the treaty creating the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics in Moscow.
reason: After winning the Civil War, the Bolsheviks needed a formal structure to bind the Soviet republics under one government.
significance: The USSR became a superpower that shaped the twentieth century until its collapse in 1991.
wikipedia: Treaty on the Creation of the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics

title: The Treaty of Lausanne recognizes modern Turkey
summary: Turkey and the Allied powers signed a peace treaty in Lausanne that replaced the Treaty of Sevres and recognized the borders of a sovereign Turkish state.
reason: Turkish victory in the War of Independence forced the Allies to negotiate new terms.
significance: It set Turkey's modern borders and confirmed a large population exchange between Greece and Turkey.

title: The Great Kanto earthquake devastates Tokyo and Yokohama
summary: A magnitude 7.9 earthquake struck the Kanto plain at midday, and fires destroyed much of Tokyo and Yokohama, killing over 100,000 people.
reason: The quake came from a rupture along the plate boundary under Sagami Bay, and lunchtime cooking fires spread among wooden houses.
significance: It was one of the deadliest earthquakes in history and was followed by massacres of Koreans in Japan.

title: The Republic of Turkey is proclaimed
summary: The Grand National Assembly proclaimed Turkey a republic and elected Mustafa Kemal as its first president.
reason: With the sultanate abolished and peace secured at Lausanne, Kemal wanted a modern secular state.
significance: It founded the modern Turkish state and launched sweeping reforms.

title: Hitler stages the Beer Hall Putsch in Munich
summary: Adolf Hitler and the Nazi party tried to seize power in Munich, starting at the Burgerbraukeller beer hall; the coup collapsed the next day when police opened fire.
reason: Hyperinflation and the occupation of the Ruhr had shaken the Weimar Republic, and Hitler hoped to copy Mussolini's march on Rome.
significance: Hitler's trial and imprisonment gave him national fame and the time to write Mein Kampf.

title: Vladimir Lenin dies
summary: Vladimir Lenin, founder of the Soviet state, died at his estate in Gorki near Moscow after a series of strokes.
reason: Lenin's health had failed since 1922, partly linked to an assassination attempt in 1918.
significance: His death opened a power struggle that Joseph Stalin won.
wikipedia: Death and state funeral of Vladimir Lenin

title: Turkey abolishes the Ottoman Caliphate
summary: The Turkish Grand National Assembly abolished the caliphate and expelled the last caliph, Abdulmejid II, and the Ottoman family from the country.
reason: Mustafa Kemal saw the caliphate as a rival center of power and an obstacle to a secular republic.
significance: It ended an institution that had led Sunni Islam for centuries.

title: John Logie Baird demonstrates television
summary: John Logie Baird gave the first public demonstration of television transmitting moving images to members of the Royal Institution in his London laboratory.
reason: Baird had worked for years on a mechanical scanning system to send live images electrically.
significance: It marked the beginning of television, which became the dominant medium of the century.
place: 22 Frith Street, Soho, London, United Kingdom

title: Robert Goddard launches the first liquid-fueled rocket
summary: Robert Goddard launched a small rocket fueled by gasoline and liquid oxygen from a farm in Auburn, Massachusetts; it flew for about two and a half seconds.
reason: Goddard believed liquid propellants could power rockets to high altitudes and eventually into space.
significance: It founded modern rocketry, which led to spaceflight and missiles.

title: Chiang Kai-shek launches the Northern Expedition
summary: The National Revolutionary Army under Chiang Kai-shek set out from Guangzhou on a military campaign to defeat the warlords and unify China.
reason: The Kuomintang, allied with the Communists and Soviet advisers, aimed to end warlord rule over most of China.
significance: It brought China under nominal Nationalist rule by 1928 and ended the Beiyang government.

title: Chiang Kai-shek purges the Communists in Shanghai
summary: Nationalist troops and gangsters loyal to Chiang Kai-shek attacked Communists and labor unions in Shanghai, killing hundreds and arresting many more.
reason: Chiang feared growing Communist power within the Nationalist movement and was backed by Shanghai business interests.
significance: It ended the First United Front and began the long Chinese Civil War.

title: Lindbergh takes off on the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight
summary: Charles Lindbergh took off from Roosevelt Field, New York, in the Spirit of St. Louis and landed in Paris about 33 hours later, the first solo nonstop flight across the Atlantic.
reason: Lindbergh was competing for the Orteig Prize for the first nonstop flight between New York and Paris.
significance: It made Lindbergh a world celebrity and sparked a boom in public interest in aviation.
place: Roosevelt Field, Long Island, United States

title: Communists rise in the Nanchang Uprising
summary: Communist-led troops under Zhou Enlai, He Long and Zhu De seized the city of Nanchang before being driven out by Nationalist forces days later.
reason: After the Nationalists' purge, the Communists decided to launch armed resistance.
significance: It is regarded as the founding of the People's Liberation Army, whose anniversary is 1 August.

title: The Jazz Singer premieres with synchronized speech
summary: Warner Bros. premiered The Jazz Singer, starring Al Jolson, in New York, the first feature film with synchronized dialogue and singing.
reason: Warner Bros. gambled on the Vitaphone sound-on-disc system to compete with larger studios.
significance: It started the talkie era and quickly ended silent cinema.
place: Warner Theatre, New York City, United States

title: Black Tuesday: the Wall Street Crash
summary: Panic selling on the New York Stock Exchange drove prices to collapse, completing the crash that had started days earlier and wiping out billions of dollars.
reason: Speculation, buying on margin and an overvalued market left investors exposed when confidence broke.
significance: The crash helped trigger the Great Depression, which spread around the world.
place: New York Stock Exchange, New York City, United States

title: Indian nationalists declare Purna Swaraj
summary: The Indian National Congress publicly celebrated its declaration of Purna Swaraj, complete independence from British rule, with oaths taken across India.
reason: Britain had failed to grant dominion status, and Congress under Jawaharlal Nehru adopted full independence as its goal.
significance: India later chose 26 January as Republic Day when its constitution took effect in 1950.

title: Clyde Tombaugh discovers Pluto
summary: Clyde Tombaugh at Lowell Observatory in Flagstaff, Arizona, identified a moving object on photographic plates, which became known as Pluto.
reason: Lowell Observatory was continuing Percival Lowell's search for a Planet X beyond Neptune.
significance: Pluto was counted as the ninth planet until it was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.

title: Gandhi begins the Salt March
summary: Mohandas Gandhi set out from Sabarmati Ashram with 78 followers on a 24-day walk to Dandi on the coast to make salt in defiance of the British salt tax.
reason: The salt tax was a symbol of British rule that hurt every Indian, making it an ideal target for civil disobedience.
significance: It drew world attention to the Indian independence movement and launched a mass civil disobedience campaign.

title: The first FIFA World Cup kicks off in Uruguay
summary: The first FIFA World Cup began with matches in Montevideo; France beat Mexico in the opening game, and Uruguay went on to win the tournament.
reason: FIFA wanted a world championship for football separate from the Olympics, and Uruguay, the Olympic champion, offered to host it.
significance: The World Cup became the most watched sporting event on Earth.

title: The Second Spanish Republic is proclaimed
summary: After republicans swept municipal elections, a republic was proclaimed in Madrid and King Alfonso XIII left Spain.
reason: The monarchy was discredited by its support of Miguel Primo de Rivera's dictatorship.
significance: The republic's deep divisions led to the Spanish Civil War five years later.

title: The Mukden Incident gives Japan a pretext to seize Manchuria
summary: Japanese officers blew up a section of railway near Mukden, blamed Chinese soldiers, and used it as a pretext for the Kwantung Army to invade Manchuria.
reason: Japanese militarists wanted Manchuria's resources and territory and acted without approval from Tokyo.
significance: It led to the puppet state of Manchukuo and exposed the League of Nations' weakness.

title: The Statute of Westminster grants dominions full independence
summary: The British Parliament passed the Statute of Westminster, giving the dominions such as Canada, Australia, New Zealand and South Africa legislative independence.
reason: The dominions had grown into nations and demanded legal equality with Britain, as recognized in the Balfour Declaration of 1926.
significance: It turned the British Empire into the Commonwealth of equal nations.

title: Japan sets up the puppet state of Manchukuo
summary: Japan proclaimed the state of Manchukuo in Manchuria, installing the former Qing emperor Puyi as its head with its capital at Changchun.
reason: After conquering Manchuria, Japan wanted a nominally independent regime to control the region's resources.
significance: It deepened conflict with China and led Japan to leave the League of Nations.

title: Siam's absolute monarchy is overthrown
summary: The Khana Ratsadon, a group of civilians and officers, staged a bloodless coup in Bangkok and forced King Prajadhipok to accept a constitution.
reason: Western-educated reformers resented royal privilege, and the Great Depression had strained the economy.
significance: It ended absolute monarchy in Siam, now Thailand.

title: Ibn Saud proclaims the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
summary: Abdulaziz Ibn Saud united his domains of the Hejaz and Nejd into a single kingdom named Saudi Arabia.
reason: After decades of conquest across the Arabian peninsula, Ibn Saud sought to consolidate his realm under one name and crown.
significance: It founded the Saudi state, which became a central power in the Middle East and the oil economy.

title: Adolf Hitler is appointed Chancellor of Germany
summary: President Paul von Hindenburg appointed Nazi party leader Adolf Hitler as Chancellor at the head of a coalition government.
reason: The Depression had fueled Nazi support, and conservative elites believed they could control Hitler.
significance: It began the Nazi dictatorship that led to World War II and the Holocaust.

title: The Reichstag building burns
summary: The German parliament building in Berlin was set on fire; a Dutch communist, Marinus van der Lubbe, was arrested at the scene.
reason: The Nazis blamed a communist plot and used the fire as a pretext for emergency measures.
significance: The Reichstag Fire Decree suspended civil liberties and paved the way for dictatorship.

title: Franklin D. Roosevelt takes office and launches the New Deal
summary: Franklin D. Roosevelt was inaugurated as US president, declaring that the only thing to fear was fear itself, and began a burst of emergency economic legislation.
reason: The Great Depression had left a quarter of workers jobless and the banking system near collapse.
significance: The New Deal reshaped the role of the US federal government in the economy.
place: United States Capitol, Washington, D.C., United States
wikipedia: First inauguration of Franklin D. Roosevelt

title: The Reichstag passes the Enabling Act
summary: Meeting in the Kroll Opera House, the Reichstag passed a law allowing Hitler's cabinet to make laws without parliament, with only the Social Democrats voting against.
reason: Hitler sought legal cover for dictatorship, using intimidation and promises to win the needed two-thirds majority.
significance: It gave Hitler dictatorial power and ended Weimar democracy.

title: Hitler purges rivals in the Night of the Long Knives
summary: Hitler had SA leader Ernst Rohm and dozens of other rivals arrested and murdered by the SS over several days, starting at Bad Wiessee.
reason: Hitler wanted to remove the SA as a threat and win the loyalty of the army.
significance: It consolidated Hitler's absolute power and established the SS as the regime's terror arm.

title: The Chinese Red Army begins the Long March
summary: Encircled by Nationalist forces, about 86,000 troops of the Red Army broke out of the Jiangxi Soviet and began a retreat of thousands of kilometers.
reason: Chiang Kai-shek's encirclement campaigns had made the Communist base in Jiangxi untenable.
significance: It saved the Chinese Communist Party and brought Mao Zedong to its leadership.

title: Nazi Germany enacts the Nuremberg Laws
summary: At the Nazi party rally in Nuremberg, the Reichstag passed laws stripping Jews of German citizenship and banning marriage between Jews and non-Jews.
reason: The Nazi regime's racial ideology aimed to exclude Jews from German society.
significance: It gave legal form to Nazi antisemitism and was a step toward the Holocaust.

title: Italy invades Ethiopia
summary: Italian troops crossed from Eritrea into Ethiopia without a declaration of war, beginning the Second Italo-Ethiopian War.
reason: Mussolini sought an empire and revenge for Italy's defeat at Adwa in 1896.
significance: The League of Nations' failure to stop the invasion discredited collective security.

title: German troops reoccupy the Rhineland
summary: German troops marched into the demilitarized Rhineland in breach of the Treaty of Versailles and the Locarno Treaties; France and Britain did not respond with force.
reason: Hitler gambled that the Western powers, divided and war-weary, would not act.
significance: Its success encouraged Hitler's later aggression and weakened France's security.

title: Military uprising starts the Spanish Civil War
summary: Army officers rose against the Spanish Republic, starting in Melilla in Spanish Morocco; the coup's partial failure led to a three-year civil war.
reason: Right-wing officers opposed the Popular Front government and feared revolution.
significance: The war ended in Franco's dictatorship and was a prelude to World War II.

title: The Berlin Olympics open
summary: Hitler opened the Summer Olympics in Berlin, where Jesse Owens won four gold medals in athletics.
reason: Nazi Germany used the Games to showcase the regime and its claims of racial superiority.
significance: The Games became a symbol of sport used as propaganda, and Owens's victories its rebuttal.

title: Chiang Kai-shek is detained in the Xi'an Incident
summary: Generals Zhang Xueliang and Yang Hucheng detained Chiang Kai-shek at Xi'an and forced him to agree to stop fighting the Communists and resist Japan.
reason: Many Chinese officers believed the war against the Communists should give way to defense against Japanese aggression.
significance: It led to the Second United Front against Japan and saved the Communists from defeat.

title: German and Italian bombers destroy Guernica
summary: Aircraft of the German Condor Legion and the Italian air force bombed the Basque town of Guernica on market day, killing hundreds of civilians.
reason: Franco's Nationalists and their allies sought to break Basque resistance and test aerial bombing tactics.
significance: It became a symbol of the horror of war against civilians, immortalized by Picasso's painting.

title: The Hindenburg airship bursts into flames
summary: The German passenger airship Hindenburg caught fire while docking at Lakehurst, New Jersey, killing 36 people in front of newsreel cameras.
reason: The airship was filled with flammable hydrogen, and a spark is thought to have ignited leaking gas.
significance: The disaster ended the era of passenger airships.
place: Naval Air Station Lakehurst, New Jersey, United States

title: Marco Polo Bridge Incident starts the Second Sino-Japanese War
summary: A clash between Japanese and Chinese troops near the Marco Polo Bridge outside Beijing escalated into full-scale war between Japan and China.
reason: Japan had been expanding into northern China, and both sides refused to back down after the skirmish.
significance: It began the Second Sino-Japanese War, which merged into World War II and killed millions.

title: Japanese troops capture Nanjing and begin the Nanjing Massacre
summary: Japanese forces took China's capital Nanjing and over the following weeks killed tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands of civilians and prisoners and committed mass rapes.
reason: Japanese commanders tolerated and encouraged brutality after fierce fighting at Shanghai.
significance: It remains one of the worst atrocities of the twentieth century and a deep wound in Chinese-Japanese relations.

title: Oil is struck in commercial quantity in Saudi Arabia
summary: American geologists of the California Arabian Standard Oil Company struck oil in commercial quantities at the Dammam No. 7 well near Dhahran.
reason: After years of dry wells, the company kept drilling deeper on the advice of geologist Max Steineke.
significance: It turned Saudi Arabia into one of the world's leading oil producers.

title: Germany annexes Austria in the Anschluss
summary: German troops crossed into Austria unopposed, and Hitler announced its union with Germany the next day.
reason: Hitler wanted to unite all Germans in one Reich, and he moved to stop Chancellor Schuschnigg's referendum on independence.
significance: It was Hitler's first annexation of a sovereign state and showed the Western powers would not resist.

title: Mexico nationalizes its oil industry
summary: President Lazaro Cardenas announced the expropriation of the assets of foreign oil companies in Mexico, leading to the creation of Pemex.
reason: The foreign companies refused to obey a Supreme Court ruling to raise workers' wages and improve conditions.
significance: It became a symbol of Mexican sovereignty and an early model for resource nationalism.

title: The Munich Agreement hands the Sudetenland to Germany
summary: Germany, Britain, France and Italy signed an agreement in Munich allowing Germany to annex the Sudetenland of Czechoslovakia, which was not consulted.
reason: Britain and France, unready for war, hoped to satisfy Hitler through appeasement.
significance: It became the classic example of failed appeasement on the road to World War II.

title: Kristallnacht pogrom across Nazi Germany
summary: Nazi paramilitaries and civilians attacked Jewish homes, shops and synagogues across Germany and Austria, killing dozens and sending about 30,000 Jewish men to concentration camps.
reason: The regime used the killing of a German diplomat in Paris by a young Polish Jew as a pretext for organized violence.
significance: It marked a shift from discrimination to open violence against Jews, foreshadowing the Holocaust.

title: Hahn and Strassmann discover nuclear fission
summary: In Berlin, Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann detected barium after bombarding uranium with neutrons, which Lise Meitner and Otto Frisch soon explained as the splitting of the nucleus.
reason: Physicists across Europe were studying what happened when uranium was bombarded with neutrons.
significance: It opened the way to nuclear power and the atomic bomb.
place: Kaiser Wilhelm Institute for Chemistry, Berlin, Germany

title: Earthquake destroys Chillan in central Chile
summary: A powerful earthquake struck south-central Chile late at night, levelling the city of Chillan and nearby towns. Around 28,000 people died, making it the deadliest earthquake in Chilean history.
reason: Chile sits on the boundary where the Nazca Plate dives beneath South America, and most houses in the region were built of heavy adobe that collapsed easily.
significance: The disaster led Chile to found CORFO, its state development agency, and to adopt stricter building codes.

title: Eugenio Pacelli is elected Pope Pius XII
summary: On his 63rd birthday, Cardinal Eugenio Pacelli was elected pope after a one-day conclave and took the name Pius XII.
reason: Pope Pius XI had died in February, and the cardinals wanted an experienced diplomat as war in Europe looked likely; Pacelli had been the Vatican's Secretary of State.
significance: He led the Catholic Church through the Second World War, and his conduct toward the Holocaust remains one of the most debated questions about the modern papacy.

title: German troops occupy Prague and Bohemia-Moravia
summary: German forces marched into the remaining Czech lands, and Hitler declared the Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia from Prague Castle. Slovakia had declared itself a separate state under German protection the day before.
reason: Hitler wanted Czech industry and territory beyond the Sudetenland he had gained at Munich, and the rump Czechoslovak state was too weak to resist.
significance: It proved the Munich Agreement worthless and turned Britain and France toward guaranteeing Poland, which set the course for war.

title: Franco declares victory in the Spanish Civil War
summary: General Francisco Franco announced that the war was over after Nationalist troops had taken Madrid and the last Republican forces had surrendered.
reason: The Republic was divided and exhausted after three years of fighting, while the Nationalists had steady support from Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy.
significance: It began Franco's dictatorship, which ruled Spain until 1975 and sent hundreds of thousands of Republicans into exile or prison.

title: Marian Anderson sings at the Lincoln Memorial
summary: The contralto Marian Anderson gave an open-air Easter Sunday concert on the steps of the Lincoln Memorial for about 75,000 people and a national radio audience.
reason: The Daughters of the American Revolution had refused to let her sing at Constitution Hall because she was Black, and Eleanor Roosevelt helped arrange the outdoor concert instead.
significance: It became a landmark of the early civil rights movement and showed the moral force of a peaceful public protest.
place: Lincoln Memorial, Washington, D.C., United States

title: Soviet-Japanese fighting begins at Khalkhin Gol
summary: Clashes between Mongolian and Manchukuoan cavalry on the disputed Khalkhin Gol river grew into a full battle between the Soviet Union and Japan. In August a Soviet offensive led by Georgy Zhukov encircled and destroyed the Japanese forces.
reason: Japan and the Soviet Union disputed the border between Japanese-controlled Manchukuo and the Soviet-allied Mongolian People's Republic.
significance: The defeat pushed Japan to turn south against European colonies rather than north against the Soviet Union, which shaped the Pacific War.
place: Khalkhin Gol river, Dornod Province, Mongolia

title: Einstein signs letter warning Roosevelt of atomic bombs
summary: Albert Einstein signed a letter drafted by Leo Szilard warning President Franklin D. Roosevelt that a uranium chain reaction could produce extremely powerful bombs and that Germany might build them.
reason: Nuclear fission had been discovered in Germany months earlier, and refugee physicists feared Hitler would gain such a weapon first.
significance: It led to the first American government research on uranium and, in time, to the Manhattan Project.
place: Nassau Point, Peconic, New York, United States

title: Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union sign a non-aggression pact
summary: Foreign ministers Joachim von Ribbentrop and Vyacheslav Molotov signed a ten-year non-aggression treaty in Moscow. A secret protocol divided Poland, the Baltic states, Finland and Romania into German and Soviet spheres of influence.
reason: Hitler wanted to attack Poland without facing a two-front war, and Stalin, distrusting Britain and France, sought time and territory.
significance: It cleared the way for the invasion of Poland a week later and the Soviet annexations that followed.

title: Germany invades Poland, starting the Second World War in Europe
summary: German forces attacked Poland from the west, north and south, and the battleship Schleswig-Holstein opened fire on the Polish depot at Westerplatte. Britain and France declared war on Germany two days later.
reason: Hitler sought to destroy Poland and gain living space in the east, and his pact with the Soviet Union had removed the threat of Soviet opposition.
significance: It began the deadliest war in history in Europe.

title: Soviet Union attacks Finland, starting the Winter War
summary: Soviet troops crossed the Finnish border and Soviet planes bombed Helsinki. The Finns held out through the winter with fierce resistance before agreeing to peace in March 1940.
reason: Stalin demanded Finnish territory near Leningrad and bases on the Gulf of Finland, and Finland refused.
significance: Finland kept its independence but lost Karelia, and the poor Soviet performance encouraged Hitler to think the Red Army was weak.
place: Helsinki and the Karelian Isthmus, Finland

title: Gone with the Wind premieres in Atlanta
summary: The film of Margaret Mitchell's novel, starring Vivien Leigh and Clark Gable, premiered at Loew's Grand Theatre in Atlanta amid three days of celebrations.
reason: Producer David O. Selznick had spent years and a record budget on the adaptation of one of the best-selling American novels.
significance: Adjusted for inflation it remains the highest-grossing film ever, and Hattie McDaniel's role in it won the first Oscar for a Black performer.
place: Loew's Grand Theatre, Atlanta, Georgia, United States

title: Earthquake devastates Erzincan in eastern Turkey
summary: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake on the North Anatolian Fault destroyed the city of Erzincan in the middle of a winter night. About 33,000 people died, many from the cold after their homes collapsed.
reason: The North Anatolian Fault is one of the most active faults in the world, where the Anatolian Plate slides past the Eurasian Plate.
significance: It was the deadliest earthquake in modern Turkish history until 1999 and began a series of large ruptures along the fault.

title: Hattie McDaniel becomes the first Black Oscar winner
summary: Hattie McDaniel won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress for Gone with the Wind. She had to sit at a separate table at the back of the segregated hotel ballroom.
reason: Her performance was widely praised, but Hollywood and the hotel still followed the racial segregation of the time.
significance: It was the first Oscar won by an African American, and no Black woman won another acting Oscar for fifty years.
participants: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
place: Ambassador Hotel, Los Angeles, California, United States

title: All-India Muslim League adopts the Lahore Resolution
summary: At its session in Lahore, the All-India Muslim League led by Muhammad Ali Jinnah called for independent states in the Muslim-majority regions of north-west and east British India.
reason: Many Muslim leaders feared they would be a permanent minority in a united India dominated by the Hindu-majority Congress.
significance: It became the founding demand for Pakistan, and 23 March is now celebrated as Pakistan Day.
place: Minto Park (now Iqbal Park), Lahore, Pakistan

title: Germany attacks France and the Low Countries
summary: German forces invaded the Netherlands, Belgium and Luxembourg, while their armoured divisions moved through the Ardennes forest and broke through at Sedan. The same day Winston Churchill became British Prime Minister.
reason: Hitler aimed to knock France out of the war quickly, and the Allies expected the main attack further north.
significance: Within six weeks France was defeated, leaving Britain alone against Germany in western Europe.

title: Dunkirk evacuation begins
summary: The Royal Navy, helped by hundreds of civilian small boats, began evacuating Allied soldiers trapped at Dunkirk. By 4 June more than 338,000 British and French troops had been brought to England.
reason: German armoured forces had cut off the British Expeditionary Force and French armies against the Channel coast.
significance: Saving the army allowed Britain to keep fighting, and the 'Dunkirk spirit' became a lasting part of British national memory.

title: France signs an armistice with Germany at Compiegne
summary: French representatives signed an armistice in the same railway carriage, in the Compiegne forest, where Germany had signed the armistice of 1918. Germany occupied northern and western France, and a collaborationist regime formed at Vichy.
reason: The French army had collapsed, Paris had fallen, and Marshal Philippe Petain's new government chose to stop fighting.
significance: It divided France for four years and left Britain and its empire as Germany's only major opponents in the west.
place: Glade of the Armistice, Compiegne, France

title: Battle of Britain begins over the English Channel
summary: The Luftwaffe began sustained attacks on British shipping and then on airfields and cities, fighting the Royal Air Force for control of the skies through the summer and autumn.
reason: Germany needed air superiority before it could attempt an invasion of Britain, which had refused to make peace.
significance: Germany's failure to defeat the RAF was Hitler's first major setback and kept Britain in the war as a base for the later liberation of Europe.
place: Southern England and the English Channel, United Kingdom

title: Leon Trotsky is fatally attacked in Mexico City
summary: The Soviet agent Ramon Mercader struck Leon Trotsky with an ice axe at his house in Coyoacan. Trotsky died in hospital the following day.
reason: Stalin had ordered the killing of his exiled rival, who had kept writing and organising against him from abroad.
significance: It removed the most prominent opponent of Stalin within the communist movement.

title: Teenagers discover the Lascaux cave paintings
summary: Four teenagers exploring a hole near Montignac in south-west France found a cave whose walls were covered with paintings of horses, bulls and deer.
reason: The boys, led by Marcel Ravidat, were following a dog, or a local legend of a hidden tunnel, into a shaft opened by a fallen tree.
significance: The roughly 17,000-year-old paintings are among the finest known works of Paleolithic art.

title: Japan invades northern French Indochina
summary: Japanese troops crossed from China into northern Vietnam and fought brief battles with French colonial forces around Lang Son before Vichy France accepted Japanese bases.
reason: Japan wanted to cut the supply route to Nationalist China through Haiphong and to gain a foothold in South-East Asia after France's defeat.
significance: It drew US economic sanctions on Japan and began the Japanese presence in Indochina that later fed the Vietnamese independence struggle.

title: Germany, Italy and Japan sign the Tripartite Pact
summary: Representatives of Germany, Italy and Japan signed a pact in Berlin promising to support each other if attacked by a power not yet in the war.
reason: The three powers wanted to deter the United States from entering the conflicts in Europe and Asia.
significance: It formally created the Axis alliance that fought the Allies in both Europe and the Pacific.

title: German authorities seal the Warsaw Ghetto
summary: The Nazi occupation authorities closed the walled Jewish district in Warsaw, trapping about 400,000 people in a small area with little food.
reason: The Nazis aimed to isolate and exploit Poland's Jews as a step in their persecution, which later turned into mass murder.
significance: The largest ghetto in occupied Europe, it became a symbol of the Holocaust; tens of thousands died there of hunger and disease.

title: Penicillin is first given to a patient in Oxford
summary: At the Radcliffe Infirmary, police constable Albert Alexander, dying of a severe infection, became the first patient treated with purified penicillin. He improved dramatically, but supplies ran out and he died weeks later.
reason: Howard Florey and Ernst Chain's team had turned Alexander Fleming's 1928 discovery into a usable drug, but could make only tiny amounts.
significance: It showed penicillin worked in people and led to the mass production that saved countless lives by the war's end.

title: Roosevelt signs the Lend-Lease Act
summary: President Franklin D. Roosevelt signed a law allowing the United States to lend or lease weapons and supplies to any country whose defence was vital to American security.
reason: Britain was running out of money to buy American arms, and Roosevelt wanted to help it without entering the war.
significance: It made the United States the 'arsenal of democracy', supplying Britain, the Soviet Union, China and others with goods worth tens of billions of dollars.
place: White House, Washington, D.C., United States

title: Citizen Kane premieres in New York
summary: Orson Welles's first feature film, about the rise and fall of a newspaper tycoon, premiered at the Palace Theatre on Broadway.
reason: Welles had been given unusual creative freedom by RKO, while the newspaper owner William Randolph Hearst, who saw himself in the story, tried to stop its release.
significance: Its storytelling and camera work made it one of the most influential films ever made, often ranked as the greatest.
place: Palace Theatre, New York City, United States

title: Haile Selassie returns to Addis Ababa
summary: Emperor Haile Selassie re-entered his capital five years to the day after Italian troops had occupied it, escorted by Ethiopian patriots and British and African forces.
reason: British Commonwealth troops and Ethiopian resistance fighters had driven the Italians out of most of Ethiopia in the East African campaign.
significance: Ethiopia became the first country occupied by the Axis to be liberated, and it regained its independence.

title: Germany invades the Soviet Union
summary: More than three million Axis soldiers attacked the Soviet Union along a front from the Baltic to the Black Sea. The Soviet defenders were caught by surprise and lost huge numbers of men and aircraft in the first weeks.
reason: Hitler wanted to destroy communism, seize land and resources in the east and wipe out the Jewish and Slavic populations there.
significance: It opened the largest and deadliest land campaign in history, where most of the German army was eventually destroyed.

title: Roosevelt bans racial discrimination in US defence industries
summary: President Roosevelt issued Executive Order 8802, forbidding discrimination by race, creed, colour or national origin in the defence industries and the federal government, and set up a committee to enforce it.
reason: A. Philip Randolph had threatened a mass march on Washington by Black workers shut out of booming war jobs.
significance: It was the first federal action against racial discrimination in employment since Reconstruction.

title: Roosevelt and Churchill issue the Atlantic Charter
summary: After meeting on warships in Placentia Bay, Newfoundland, Roosevelt and Churchill published a joint statement of goals for the world after the war, including self-determination, free trade and no territorial gains.
reason: Roosevelt wanted to define shared aims with Britain even though the United States was not yet at war.
significance: Its principles became the basis of the Declaration by United Nations and later the United Nations Charter.

title: Britain and the Soviet Union invade Iran
summary: British and Soviet forces entered Iran from the south and north and overcame its army within days. Reza Shah was forced to abdicate in favour of his son Mohammad Reza Pahlavi.
reason: The Allies wanted Iran's oil fields and a supply route to the Soviet Union, and distrusted the Shah's ties to Germany.
significance: The Persian Corridor became a key Lend-Lease route, and the occupation deeply shaped Iranian nationalism.

title: Siege of Leningrad begins
summary: German and Finnish forces cut the last land route to Leningrad, beginning a blockade that lasted almost 900 days. Around a million civilians died, most of them from starvation in the winter of 1941 to 1942.
reason: Hitler chose to starve the city rather than storm it, aiming to wipe it out.
significance: It was one of the longest and deadliest sieges in history and a lasting symbol of Soviet endurance.

title: Babi Yar massacre of the Jews of Kyiv
summary: Over two days, German SS units and police, aided by local collaborators, shot 33,771 Jews in the Babi Yar ravine on the edge of Kyiv.
reason: It was part of the mass shootings of Jews that followed the German invasion of the Soviet Union.
significance: It was one of the largest single massacres of the Holocaust.

title: Japan attacks Pearl Harbor
summary: Japanese carrier aircraft struck the US Pacific Fleet at Pearl Harbor in Hawaii, sinking or damaging eight battleships and killing about 2,400 Americans.
reason: Japan wanted to cripple the US fleet so it could seize the resource-rich colonies of South-East Asia after the United States cut off its oil.
significance: It brought the United States into the Second World War and turned the conflict into a truly global war.
place: Pearl Harbor, Oahu, Hawaii, United States

title: Japan lands in Malaya at Kota Bharu
summary: Japanese troops landed at Kota Bharu in north-east Malaya and in southern Thailand, shortly before the attack on Pearl Harbor. They then advanced quickly down the peninsula toward Singapore.
reason: Japan wanted the rubber and tin of British Malaya and the naval base of Singapore.
significance: It began Japan's conquest of South-East Asia and the collapse of British power in the region.

title: Hong Kong surrenders to Japan
summary: After eighteen days of fighting, the British governor surrendered Hong Kong to Japanese forces on Christmas Day, known locally as Black Christmas.
reason: Japan attacked the British colony as part of its offensive across Asia, and the small garrison could not be relieved.
significance: It began nearly four years of harsh Japanese occupation in Hong Kong.

title: Nazi officials coordinate the Holocaust at Wannsee
summary: Senior Nazi and German government officials met in a villa at Wannsee, Berlin, under Reinhard Heydrich to coordinate the deportation and murder of the Jews of Europe.
reason: Mass killing was already under way, and Heydrich wanted all ministries to cooperate in what the Nazis called the Final Solution.
significance: Its minutes are among the clearest records of the Holocaust's planning.

title: Singapore falls to Japan
summary: General Arthur Percival surrendered Singapore and about 80,000 British, Indian and Australian troops to the Japanese army of Tomoyuki Yamashita.
reason: Japanese forces had swept through Malaya, and the island's defences were not designed for an attack from the north.
significance: Churchill called it the worst disaster in British military history, and it badly damaged British prestige in Asia.

title: Roosevelt orders the removal of Japanese Americans
summary: President Roosevelt signed Executive Order 9066, allowing the military to exclude people from areas of the West Coast. About 120,000 people of Japanese descent, most of them US citizens, were sent to camps.
reason: Fear and racial prejudice after Pearl Harbor led officials to treat Japanese Americans as a security threat without evidence.
significance: It became one of the gravest civil rights violations in US history, for which the government formally apologised in 1988.

title: Bataan surrender leads to the Bataan Death March
summary: About 76,000 American and Filipino troops surrendered on the Bataan peninsula and were forced to march some 100 kilometres to prison camps. Thousands died from beatings, heat and lack of water.
reason: The defenders had held out for three months without supplies or reinforcements, and the Japanese were unprepared for so many prisoners.
significance: It was the largest surrender of US forces in history and became a symbol of Japanese war crimes.
participants: United States Army Forces in the Far East

title: Battle of Midway turns the tide in the Pacific
summary: US carrier aircraft sank four Japanese fleet carriers near Midway Atoll, losing only one of their own.
reason: Japan planned to lure the remaining US carriers into a trap, but American codebreakers had read its plans.
significance: It destroyed the core of Japan's carrier force and shifted the initiative in the Pacific to the United States.

title: US Marines land on Guadalcanal
summary: US Marines landed on Guadalcanal and nearby islands in the Solomons, beginning a six-month campaign of land, sea and air battles.
reason: The Allies wanted to stop Japan from using an airfield on the island to cut the supply line between the United States and Australia.
significance: It was the first major Allied offensive against Japan and ended Japanese expansion in the South Pacific.

title: Gandhi launches the Quit India Movement
summary: At a session in Bombay, the Indian National Congress passed a resolution demanding an immediate end to British rule, and Gandhi urged Indians to 'do or die'. The British arrested the Congress leaders the next morning, and mass protests followed.
reason: Talks over Indian self-government had failed, and Congress refused to support a war it had not been consulted about.
significance: It was the largest challenge to British rule since 1857 and showed that India could not be held indefinitely.

title: First successful V-2 rocket launch at Peenemunde
summary: A German A-4 rocket, later called the V-2, flew about 190 kilometres from Peenemunde and reached the edge of space.
reason: The German army had funded Wernher von Braun's rocket programme as a long-range weapon not limited by the Versailles Treaty.
significance: It was the first human-made object to reach space, and its technology later fed both Soviet and American space programmes.

title: Second Battle of El Alamein begins
summary: The British Eighth Army under Bernard Montgomery attacked the German and Italian forces of Erwin Rommel in the Egyptian desert, breaking through after twelve days.
reason: Rommel's advance threatened the Suez Canal and Middle East oil, and the British had built up a large superiority in men and tanks.
significance: It ended the Axis threat to Egypt and was Britain's first major land victory over Germany.

title: First controlled nuclear chain reaction in Chicago
summary: A team led by Enrico Fermi achieved the first self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction in Chicago Pile-1, a stack of graphite and uranium under the stands of a football field at the University of Chicago.
reason: The Manhattan Project needed proof that a chain reaction could be started and controlled before building reactors and bombs.
significance: It opened the nuclear age, leading both to atomic weapons and to nuclear power.
place: University of Chicago, Chicago, Illinois, United States

title: Casablanca Conference opens in Morocco
summary: Roosevelt and Churchill met at Anfa near Casablanca to plan Allied strategy, agreeing to invade Sicily and to demand the unconditional surrender of the Axis powers.
reason: With North Africa almost won, the Allies needed to decide where to fight next and to reassure the Soviet Union.
significance: The demand for unconditional surrender shaped the rest of the war and how it ended.

title: German Sixth Army surrenders at Stalingrad
summary: The last German troops encircled in Stalingrad surrendered, ending a five-month battle. About 91,000 survivors were taken prisoner.
reason: Hitler had forbidden a breakout after the Red Army encircled the Sixth Army in November 1942, and relief attempts failed.
significance: It was a turning point of the war in Europe, after which Germany was mostly on the defensive in the east.

title: Paricutin volcano erupts out of a Mexican cornfield
summary: A farmer named Dionisio Pulido saw the ground crack open and smoke in his cornfield in Michoacan. Within a week a cone more than 100 metres high had formed, and lava later buried two villages.
reason: The area lies in a volcanic field above the subducting Cocos Plate, where magma found a new path to the surface.
significance: It was the first time scientists could study the birth and full life of a volcano from its first day.

title: Warsaw Ghetto Uprising begins
summary: When German forces entered the Warsaw Ghetto to deport its remaining Jews, armed Jewish fighters resisted. They held out for almost a month before the Germans burned the ghetto block by block.
reason: Most of the ghetto's people had already been sent to Treblinka, and the survivors knew deportation meant death.
significance: It was the largest Jewish revolt of the Holocaust and became a lasting symbol of resistance.

title: Axis forces in North Africa surrender in Tunisia
summary: The last German and Italian forces in Tunisia surrendered to the Allies, and about 250,000 soldiers became prisoners.
reason: Squeezed between the British advancing from Libya and the Americans and British from Algeria, the Axis armies had no way to escape by sea.
significance: It ended the North African campaign and opened the way for the invasion of Italy.

title: Battle of Kursk begins
summary: Germany launched Operation Citadel against the Soviet salient around Kursk, leading to one of the largest tank battles in history. The Red Army absorbed the attack and then counterattacked.
reason: Hitler hoped a victory would regain the initiative after Stalingrad, but the Soviets knew the plan and had built deep defences.
significance: It was Germany's last major offensive in the east, after which the Red Army advanced almost without pause.

title: Allies land in Sicily
summary: British, Canadian and American troops landed on the southern coast of Sicily, beginning a campaign that took the island in five weeks.
reason: After victory in North Africa the Allies chose Sicily to open the Mediterranean and knock Italy out of the war.
significance: It led directly to the fall of Mussolini and to the Allied invasion of mainland Italy.

title: Mussolini is deposed and arrested
summary: After the Grand Council of Fascism voted against him, King Victor Emmanuel III dismissed Benito Mussolini and had him arrested, naming Marshal Pietro Badoglio as head of government.
reason: Military defeats, the invasion of Sicily and bombing of Italian cities had destroyed support for Mussolini even among Fascist leaders.
significance: It ended over twenty years of Fascist rule and led Italy to surrender to the Allies in September.
wikipedia: Fall of the Fascist regime in Italy

title: Subhas Chandra Bose proclaims the Azad Hind government
summary: In Japanese-occupied Singapore, Subhas Chandra Bose proclaimed the Provisional Government of Free India and took command of the Indian National Army.
reason: Bose believed India could win independence by fighting Britain alongside the Axis powers.
significance: Though it failed militarily, the later trials of its soldiers stirred Indian nationalism and hastened the end of British rule.

title: Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin meet in Tehran
summary: The leaders of the United States, Britain and the Soviet Union met together for the first time, at the Soviet embassy in Tehran.
reason: Stalin had long demanded a second front in western Europe, and the Allies needed to agree on strategy for the final phase of the war.
significance: They agreed on the invasion of France in 1944 and began shaping the post-war order.

title: Japan launches its offensive on Imphal
summary: The Japanese army crossed the Chindwin river to attack British and Indian forces at Imphal and Kohima in north-east India. Besieged but supplied by air, the defenders held, and the Japanese retreated with enormous losses.
reason: Japan hoped to stop an Allied offensive into Burma and perhaps spark an uprising in India.
significance: It was Japan's greatest land defeat to that point and opened the way for the reconquest of Burma.

title: Soviet Union deports the Crimean Tatars
summary: Soviet security forces rounded up the entire Crimean Tatar people, about 190,000 people, and sent them in cattle cars to Central Asia. Many thousands died on the way and in the first years of exile.
reason: Stalin accused the whole nation of collaborating with the German occupiers.
significance: Ukraine and several other countries recognise it as a genocide, and the Tatars could return only after 1989.

title: D-Day: Allied forces land in Normandy
summary: About 156,000 American, British, Canadian and other Allied troops landed on five beaches in Normandy, supported by paratroopers and thousands of ships and aircraft.
reason: The Allies needed a second front in western Europe to defeat Germany, and had spent years preparing the largest seaborne invasion in history.
significance: It began the liberation of western Europe and sealed Nazi Germany's defeat.

title: Bretton Woods Conference opens
summary: Delegates from 44 Allied nations met at the Mount Washington Hotel in Bretton Woods to design the post-war international monetary system.
reason: Leaders wanted to avoid the currency wars and depression of the 1930s that had helped cause the war.
significance: It created the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank and fixed exchange rates to the US dollar for a generation.
participants: United Nations Monetary and Financial Conference
place: Mount Washington Hotel, Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, United States

title: Warsaw Uprising begins
summary: The Polish Home Army rose against the German occupiers in Warsaw. After 63 days of fighting it surrendered, and the Germans destroyed most of the city.
reason: The Polish underground wanted to free Warsaw itself before the approaching Red Army arrived, to secure Poland's independence.
significance: About 200,000 Poles died, and the Soviet Union's failure to help remains a bitter memory in Poland.

title: Anne Frank and her family are arrested in Amsterdam
summary: German police raided the secret annex behind Otto Frank's business on the Prinsengracht and arrested the eight Jews who had hidden there for two years. Anne Frank died at Bergen-Belsen months later.
reason: Someone had betrayed the hiding place to the authorities, who were deporting the Jews of the Netherlands to the death camps.
significance: Her diary, saved by a helper and published in 1947, became one of the most widely read accounts of the Holocaust.

title: Paris is liberated
summary: The German commander of Paris, Dietrich von Choltitz, surrendered to French and American forces after an uprising by the French Resistance. Charles de Gaulle addressed crowds at the Hotel de Ville that evening.
reason: The Allied breakout from Normandy had reached the Seine, and the Resistance rose in the city on 19 August.
significance: It restored French self-government and made de Gaulle the leader of liberated France.

title: MacArthur returns to the Philippines at Leyte
summary: American forces landed on the island of Leyte, and General Douglas MacArthur waded ashore to announce his return to the Philippines.
reason: The United States wanted to cut Japan off from its oil sources in South-East Asia and keep MacArthur's promise to return.
significance: It began the liberation of the Philippines and led to the Battle of Leyte Gulf, the largest naval battle in history.

title: Soviet troops liberate Auschwitz
summary: Soldiers of the Red Army entered the Auschwitz camps and found about 7,000 sick and starving prisoners left behind after the SS had forced most others on death marches.
reason: The Soviet offensive across Poland reached the camp as German forces retreated westward.
significance: About 1.1 million people, most of them Jews, had been murdered there, and the date is now International Holocaust Remembrance Day.

title: Yalta Conference opens in Crimea
summary: Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin met at the Livadia Palace near Yalta to decide on the future of Germany, Poland and the planned United Nations.
reason: With Germany's defeat near, the Allies needed to agree on how to occupy it and what would happen to the liberated countries of eastern Europe.
significance: Its agreements shaped the post-war division of Europe and are often seen as the start of the Cold War order.

title: Arab League is founded in Cairo
summary: Egypt, Iraq, Transjordan, Lebanon, Saudi Arabia, Syria and Yemen signed the pact founding the League of Arab States.
reason: Arab leaders wanted closer cooperation as colonial rule weakened, and to coordinate their position on Palestine.
significance: It became the main regional organisation of the Arab world.

title: Adolf Hitler kills himself in Berlin
summary: As Soviet troops fought their way into central Berlin, Hitler shot himself in his bunker beneath the Reich Chancellery, and Eva Braun took poison.
reason: Germany had lost the war and Hitler refused to be captured.
significance: His death removed the last obstacle to Germany's surrender a week later.

title: Setif massacre begins in French Algeria
summary: A victory parade in Setif turned violent when police tried to seize Algerian nationalist flags, and riots killed about a hundred Europeans. French forces and settler militias then killed thousands of Algerians in reprisals over the following weeks.
reason: Algerian nationalists hoped the Allied victory would bring freedom, while the colonial authorities were determined to suppress them.
significance: It radicalised Algerian nationalism and is seen as a prelude to the Algerian War of Independence.

title: Germany surrenders: Victory in Europe Day
summary: The German unconditional surrender took effect, and the Allies celebrated Victory in Europe. A final surrender document was signed late that evening in Berlin-Karlshorst.
reason: Hitler was dead, Berlin had fallen and German armies had collapsed on every front.
significance: It ended the Second World War in Europe after almost six years.

title: United Nations Charter is signed in San Francisco
summary: Delegates of 50 nations signed the Charter of the United Nations at the end of a two-month conference in San Francisco.
reason: The Allies wanted a stronger organisation than the failed League of Nations to keep peace after the war.
significance: It created the United Nations, the main forum of international cooperation ever since.
participants: United Nations Conference on International Organization
place: Veterans Building, San Francisco, California, United States

title: Trinity: the first atomic bomb is detonated
summary: Scientists of the Manhattan Project exploded a plutonium bomb in the New Mexico desert, releasing energy equal to about 21,000 tons of TNT.
reason: The United States needed to test the complex implosion design before using such a weapon against Japan.
significance: It began the nuclear age, and the same design was used on Nagasaki three weeks later.
place: Jornada del Muerto desert, New Mexico, United States

title: United States drops an atomic bomb on Hiroshima
summary: The B-29 Enola Gay dropped a uranium bomb on Hiroshima, destroying most of the city and killing about 70,000 to 80,000 people at once, with many more dying later. A second bomb destroyed Nagasaki three days later.
reason: US leaders wanted to force Japan to surrender without an invasion of its home islands.
significance: It was the first use of a nuclear weapon in war and shaped international politics for the rest of the century.
wikipedia: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki

title: Emperor Hirohito announces Japan's surrender
summary: In a radio broadcast, the first time most Japanese had heard his voice, Emperor Hirohito told his people that Japan would accept the Allied terms of surrender.
reason: Japan had been hit by two atomic bombs and a Soviet invasion of Manchuria, and the emperor broke the deadlock in his cabinet.
significance: It effectively ended the Second World War, and the day is marked as liberation day in Korea.

title: Sukarno proclaims Indonesia's independence
summary: Sukarno read a short proclamation of independence at his house in Jakarta, with Mohammad Hatta at his side.
reason: Japan had just surrendered, and nationalist youths pushed the leaders to act before the Dutch could return to their former colony.
significance: It began the Indonesian National Revolution, and the Netherlands recognised Indonesia's independence in 1949.

title: Ho Chi Minh declares Vietnam's independence
summary: Before a huge crowd in Ba Dinh Square in Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh read a declaration founding the Democratic Republic of Vietnam, quoting the American Declaration of Independence.
reason: The Viet Minh had seized power in the August Revolution after Japan's surrender left a vacuum in French Indochina.
significance: France's attempt to return led to the First Indochina War and decades of conflict in Vietnam.
wikipedia: Declaration of independence of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam

title: Japan signs the surrender aboard USS Missouri
summary: Japanese officials signed the Instrument of Surrender aboard the battleship USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay, accepted by General Douglas MacArthur for the Allies.
reason: Japan's government had accepted the Potsdam terms in August after the atomic bombings and the Soviet entry into the war.
significance: It formally ended the Second World War.

title: Nuremberg trials of major Nazi leaders begin
summary: An international military tribunal of the United States, Britain, France and the Soviet Union opened the trial of 24 leading Nazis for crimes against peace, war crimes and crimes against humanity.
reason: The Allies chose a legal process instead of summary executions to establish the record of Nazi crimes and hold leaders personally responsible.
significance: It founded modern international criminal law and the principle that following orders is no defence.

title: Churchill gives the Iron Curtain speech
summary: Winston Churchill, speaking at Westminster College in Fulton, Missouri, warned that an iron curtain had descended across Europe. He called for close cooperation between Britain and the United States.
reason: Soviet control was hardening over the states of Eastern Europe occupied by the Red Army, and Churchill wanted to rally American opinion against it.
significance: The speech became one of the defining statements of the early Cold War.
place: Westminster College, Fulton, Missouri, United States

title: The Philippines becomes independent from the United States
summary: The United States recognized the independence of the Philippines in a ceremony in Manila, and the Treaty of Manila was signed the same day. Manuel Roxas became the first president of the independent republic.
reason: The Tydings-McDuffie Act of 1934 had promised independence after a ten year transition, delayed only by the Japanese occupation.
significance: It was one of the first decolonizations of the postwar era in Asia.

title: Direct Action Day riots break out in Calcutta
summary: A general strike called by the Muslim League in Calcutta turned into mass violence between Muslims and Hindus. Thousands of people were killed in the following days.
reason: The Muslim League called the protest to press its demand for a separate Muslim homeland, Pakistan.
significance: The killings made partition of India far more likely.

title: Japan promulgates its postwar constitution
summary: Emperor Hirohito promulgated a new constitution that made sovereignty rest with the people and renounced war in its Article 9. It took effect in May 1947.
reason: The American occupation authorities under Douglas MacArthur pushed for a democratic charter to replace the Meiji Constitution.
significance: It has remained Japan's constitution without a single amendment.

title: Fighting in Hanoi opens the First Indochina War
summary: Viet Minh forces attacked French positions in Hanoi, turning months of tension into open war. Ho Chi Minh and his government withdrew to the countryside.
reason: France sought to restore colonial rule in Indochina, while the Viet Minh had declared Vietnamese independence in 1945.
significance: It began the eight year war that ended French rule in Indochina.

title: Truman announces the Truman Doctrine
summary: President Harry Truman asked Congress for aid to Greece and Turkey and declared that the United States would support free peoples resisting subjugation.
reason: Britain could no longer afford to support Greece against a communist insurgency, and Turkey faced Soviet pressure.
significance: It made containment of communism the core of American foreign policy.
place: United States Capitol, Washington, D.C., United States

title: George Marshall proposes the Marshall Plan
summary: In a speech at Harvard University, Secretary of State George Marshall proposed large scale American aid to rebuild Europe.
reason: Europe was struggling with hunger and ruined economies, and Washington feared that poverty would help communist parties.
significance: The plan financed Western Europe's recovery and deepened the split with the Soviet bloc.
place: Harvard University, Cambridge, Massachusetts, United States

title: Pakistan is created as an independent state
summary: Pakistan came into being as a separate dominion for the Muslim majority areas of British India, with Muhammad Ali Jinnah as governor general.
reason: The Muslim League had demanded a separate homeland, and Britain agreed to partition the subcontinent.
significance: Partition caused one of the largest migrations in history and lasting conflict with India.

title: India becomes independent
summary: At midnight British rule ended and India became an independent dominion, with Jawaharlal Nehru as prime minister. He marked it with his Tryst with Destiny speech.
reason: Decades of nationalist struggle and a Britain exhausted by war led to a quick transfer of power, together with partition.
significance: It ended the British Raj and began the end of European empires in Asia.

title: Kashmir's maharaja accedes to India
summary: Maharaja Hari Singh of Jammu and Kashmir signed the Instrument of Accession to India as tribal fighters from Pakistan advanced toward Srinagar.
reason: The princely state had stayed undecided at partition until the invasion forced the ruler to seek Indian military help.
significance: It began the Kashmir conflict that still divides India and Pakistan.

title: The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade is signed
summary: Twenty three countries signed the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade in Geneva, cutting tariffs on a large share of world trade.
reason: Governments wanted to avoid the protectionism that had deepened the Great Depression.
significance: GATT set the rules of world trade until it became the World Trade Organization.
participants: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade
wikipedia: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade

title: UN votes to partition Palestine
summary: The United Nations General Assembly adopted Resolution 181, recommending that Mandatory Palestine be divided into Jewish and Arab states with Jerusalem under international control.
reason: Britain had given up the mandate, and the UN sought a solution to the conflicting claims of Jews and Arabs.
significance: The vote led directly to the creation of Israel and the first Arab-Israeli war.
place: Flushing Meadows, New York, United States
wikipedia: United Nations Partition Plan for Palestine

title: The transistor is demonstrated at Bell Labs
summary: John Bardeen and Walter Brattain, working in William Shockley's group, demonstrated the first working point contact transistor to Bell Labs managers.
reason: Bell Labs wanted a smaller, more reliable replacement for vacuum tubes in telephone amplifiers.
significance: The transistor became the building block of all modern electronics.
place: Bell Labs, Murray Hill, New Jersey, United States

title: Mahatma Gandhi is assassinated
summary: Nathuram Godse, a Hindu nationalist, shot Mahatma Gandhi at Birla House in New Delhi as he walked to a prayer meeting.
reason: Godse blamed Gandhi for partition and for being too accommodating toward Muslims and Pakistan.
significance: The death of the leader of Indian independence shocked the world and discredited militant Hindu nationalism for a time.

title: Assassination of Gaitan sparks the Bogotazo
summary: The popular Liberal leader Jorge Eliecer Gaitan was shot in Bogota, setting off riots that destroyed much of the city centre and killed thousands.
reason: Gaitan was the hope of poor Colombians, and political violence between Liberals and Conservatives was already rising.
significance: It opened La Violencia, a decade of civil conflict in Colombia.

title: David Ben-Gurion declares the State of Israel
summary: In Tel Aviv, David Ben-Gurion proclaimed the establishment of the State of Israel, hours before the British Mandate ended. Neighbouring Arab states invaded the next day.
reason: The UN partition plan and the end of British rule opened the way to a Jewish state.
significance: Israel's founding reshaped the Middle East and began the displacement of hundreds of thousands of Palestinians.

title: National Party wins South Africa's election
summary: The Afrikaner National Party under Daniel Malan won South Africa's general election on a programme of apartheid.
reason: White voters, especially Afrikaners, feared the growth of black urban populations and backed strict racial separation.
significance: The result began more than four decades of apartheid laws.

title: The Manchester Baby runs the first stored program
summary: The Small-Scale Experimental Machine at the University of Manchester ran its first program, held in its own electronic memory.
reason: Frederic Williams and Tom Kilburn built it to test a new kind of memory based on cathode ray tubes.
significance: It was the first stored program computer, the design of nearly every computer since.
place: University of Manchester, Manchester, United Kingdom

title: The Soviet Union begins the Berlin Blockade
summary: Soviet forces cut all road, rail and canal routes into the western sectors of Berlin. The Western Allies answered with an airlift that supplied the city for almost a year.
reason: Moscow opposed the introduction of a new currency in the western zones and wanted to push the Allies out of Berlin.
significance: It was the first major crisis of the Cold War and hastened the division of Germany.

title: The UN adopts the Universal Declaration of Human Rights
summary: Meeting at the Palais de Chaillot in Paris, the UN General Assembly adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights without a vote against.
reason: After the atrocities of the Second World War, a committee led by Eleanor Roosevelt drafted a common standard of rights for all peoples.
significance: It became the foundation of international human rights law.

title: The North Atlantic Treaty founds NATO
summary: Twelve countries of North America and Western Europe signed the North Atlantic Treaty in Washington, agreeing that an attack on one would be an attack on all.
reason: The Berlin Blockade and the communist takeover in Czechoslovakia convinced Western governments they needed a military alliance.
significance: NATO became the central Western alliance of the Cold War and after.

title: West Germany's Basic Law is promulgated
summary: The Basic Law, the constitution of the Federal Republic of Germany, was signed and promulgated in Bonn.
reason: The Western Allies wanted a democratic West German state, created from their occupation zones.
significance: It founded West Germany and remains the constitution of reunified Germany.
wikipedia: Basic Law for the Federal Republic of Germany

title: George Orwell publishes Nineteen Eighty-Four
summary: Secker and Warburg published George Orwell's novel about a totalitarian state that watches and controls its citizens.
reason: Orwell drew on his experience of Stalinism, Nazism and wartime propaganda.
significance: Its words, such as Big Brother, became the vocabulary of debate about surveillance and tyranny.

title: The Geneva Conventions are adopted
summary: A diplomatic conference in Geneva adopted four conventions protecting wounded soldiers, shipwrecked sailors, prisoners of war and civilians in wartime.
reason: The mass killing of civilians and prisoners in the Second World War showed the gaps in earlier treaties.
significance: They are the core of international humanitarian law.
participants: International Committee of the Red Cross

title: The Soviet Union tests its first atomic bomb
summary: The Soviet Union secretly exploded its first atomic bomb, RDS-1, at the Semipalatinsk test site in Kazakhstan.
reason: Stalin had ordered a crash programme after Hiroshima, helped by espionage on the Manhattan Project.
significance: It ended the American nuclear monopoly and started the nuclear arms race.

title: Mao Zedong proclaims the People's Republic of China
summary: From the Gate of Heavenly Peace in Beijing, Mao Zedong proclaimed the founding of the People's Republic of China.
reason: The Communists had won the civil war against Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists, who retreated to Taiwan.
significance: It brought the world's most populous country under communist rule.
wikipedia: Proclamation of the People's Republic of China

title: The Constitution of India comes into force
summary: India's constitution took effect, turning the dominion into a sovereign republic with Rajendra Prasad as its first president.
reason: A Constituent Assembly chaired in drafting by B. R. Ambedkar had worked since 1946 to give India its own charter.
significance: It made India the largest democracy in the world, marked each year as Republic Day.

title: Robert Schuman proposes pooling coal and steel
summary: French foreign minister Robert Schuman proposed placing French and German coal and steel production under a common authority open to other European countries.
reason: Jean Monnet's plan aimed to make another war between France and Germany materially impossible.
significance: It is seen as the founding act of European integration, marked as Europe Day.

title: North Korea invades South Korea
summary: North Korean forces crossed the 38th parallel in a full scale invasion of South Korea, quickly advancing toward Seoul.
reason: Kim Il Sung wanted to unify Korea by force and had won the approval of Stalin and Mao.
significance: The Korean War drew in the United States, the UN and China and froze the division of Korea.

title: Japan signs the Treaty of San Francisco
summary: Japan and 48 nations signed the peace treaty that formally ended the Second World War in the Pacific and restored Japan's sovereignty.
reason: The United States wanted Japan as a Cold War ally and pushed for a quick, lenient peace.
significance: It ended the occupation and shaped the postwar order in East Asia.
place: War Memorial Opera House, San Francisco, United States

title: Free Officers overthrow King Farouk
summary: The Free Officers Movement, led by Mohamed Naguib and Gamal Abdel Nasser, seized power in Egypt and forced King Farouk to abdicate.
reason: Officers were angered by corruption, British influence and Egypt's defeat in the 1948 war.
significance: It began an era of Arab nationalism led by Nasser.

title: The United States detonates the first hydrogen bomb
summary: The United States exploded Ivy Mike, the first full scale thermonuclear device, on Elugelab island in Enewetak Atoll, which was vaporized.
reason: After the first Soviet atomic test, Truman ordered development of a far more powerful weapon.
significance: It raised the nuclear arms race to weapons of almost unlimited power.

title: Joseph Stalin dies
summary: Soviet leader Joseph Stalin died at his dacha at Kuntsevo near Moscow, days after a stroke.
reason: Stalin was 74 and had been in failing health.
significance: His death opened a power struggle and a gradual thaw in the Soviet Union.
wikipedia: Death and state funeral of Joseph Stalin

title: Watson and Crick publish the structure of DNA
summary: Nature published James Watson and Francis Crick's paper proposing the double helix structure of DNA, alongside papers from King's College London.
reason: Rosalind Franklin's X-ray images and Maurice Wilkins' work gave the evidence the Cambridge pair used to build their model.
significance: It explained how genetic information is copied and founded molecular biology.
wikipedia: Molecular Structure of Nucleic Acids: A Structure for Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid

title: Hillary and Tenzing reach the summit of Everest
summary: Edmund Hillary of New Zealand and Tenzing Norgay, a Sherpa from Nepal, became the first people known to reach the top of Mount Everest.
reason: A large British expedition led by John Hunt had chosen them for the second summit attempt.
significance: It was the climax of the race for the world's highest peak.

title: The Korean Armistice ends the fighting in Korea
summary: Delegates of the UN Command, North Korea and the Chinese volunteers signed an armistice at Panmunjom, creating a demilitarized zone.
reason: Two years of stalemate and Stalin's death made both sides ready to stop fighting.
significance: No peace treaty followed, so Korea remains divided and technically at war.

title: A CIA backed coup ousts Iran's Mosaddegh
summary: Royalist officers and street crowds organized with American and British help overthrew Prime Minister Mohammad Mosaddegh, restoring the shah's power.
reason: Mosaddegh had nationalized the Anglo-Iranian Oil Company, and Washington feared a communist drift.
significance: The coup shaped Iranian anger at the West that erupted in 1979.

title: Dien Bien Phu falls to the Viet Minh
summary: After a siege of nearly two months, the French garrison at Dien Bien Phu in northern Vietnam surrendered to Viet Minh forces under Vo Nguyen Giap.
reason: France had fortified the remote valley to lure the Viet Minh into battle, but Giap surrounded it with artillery on the hills.
significance: The defeat ended French rule in Indochina and sent shock waves through colonial empires.

title: US Supreme Court rules school segregation unconstitutional
summary: In Brown v. Board of Education, the Supreme Court unanimously ruled that racial segregation in public schools violated the Constitution.
reason: The NAACP, led in court by Thurgood Marshall, had challenged the separate but equal doctrine for years.
significance: The ruling was a turning point of the civil rights movement.
participants: Supreme Court of the United States
place: Supreme Court Building, Washington, D.C., United States

title: Obninsk becomes the first nuclear plant to power a grid
summary: The nuclear power plant at Obninsk near Moscow was connected to the electricity grid, the first in the world to do so.
reason: Soviet scientists wanted to show a peaceful use of atomic energy.
significance: It began the age of civil nuclear power.

title: Geneva Accords divide Vietnam
summary: The Geneva Conference ended with agreements that divided Vietnam at the 17th parallel and confirmed the independence of Laos and Cambodia.
reason: France wanted out of Indochina after Dien Bien Phu, and the great powers sought a settlement.
significance: The temporary division of Vietnam led to the Vietnam War.

title: The FLN launches the Algerian War
summary: The National Liberation Front carried out a wave of coordinated attacks across Algeria, known as Red All Saints' Day.
reason: Algerian nationalists had lost hope of reform after decades of French settler rule.
significance: It began the war that ended with Algerian independence in 1962.

title: Salk's polio vaccine is declared safe and effective
summary: At the University of Michigan, researchers announced that a huge field trial had shown Jonas Salk's polio vaccine to be safe and effective.
reason: Polio epidemics paralysed thousands of children each year, and the March of Dimes funded the trial.
significance: Mass vaccination began, and polio was eventually eliminated in most of the world.
place: University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, United States

title: The Bandung Conference opens
summary: Leaders of 29 Asian and African countries met at Bandung in Indonesia to promote cooperation and oppose colonialism.
reason: Newly independent states wanted a voice outside the rival Cold War blocs.
significance: It laid the ground for the Non-Aligned Movement.

title: The Warsaw Pact is signed
summary: The Soviet Union and seven Eastern European states signed a treaty of mutual defence in Warsaw.
reason: Moscow answered West Germany's entry into NATO with an alliance of its own.
significance: It bound the Eastern bloc militarily to Moscow until 1991.

title: The Congress of the People adopts the Freedom Charter
summary: At Kliptown near Johannesburg, the Congress of the People adopted the Freedom Charter, declaring that South Africa belongs to all who live in it.
reason: The African National Congress and its allies wanted a common programme against apartheid.
significance: The charter became the founding document of the anti-apartheid movement.

title: Rosa Parks refuses to give up her bus seat
summary: Rosa Parks, a Black seamstress and NAACP activist, was arrested in Montgomery, Alabama, for refusing to give her bus seat to a white passenger.
reason: Montgomery's buses enforced racial segregation, and activists were looking for a case to challenge it.
significance: Her arrest started the Montgomery bus boycott and brought Martin Luther King Jr. to the fore.

title: Khrushchev denounces Stalin in the Secret Speech
summary: At a closed session of the 20th Party Congress, Nikita Khrushchev condemned Stalin's personality cult and crimes.
reason: Khrushchev wanted to break with terror and strengthen his position against Stalin's old associates.
significance: The speech shook communist movements worldwide and encouraged unrest in Eastern Europe.
participants: Communist Party of the Soviet Union
wikipedia: On the Cult of Personality and Its Consequences

title: Nasser nationalizes the Suez Canal
summary: In a speech in Alexandria, Gamal Abdel Nasser announced the nationalization of the Suez Canal Company.
reason: The United States and Britain had withdrawn funding for the Aswan High Dam, and Nasser wanted canal revenue to pay for it.
significance: It led to the Suez Crisis, which marked the end of Britain and France as imperial powers in the Middle East.

title: The Hungarian Revolution begins
summary: A student demonstration in Budapest grew into a national uprising against the communist government and Soviet control. Soviet forces crushed it in November.
reason: Khrushchev's denunciation of Stalin and the Polish October encouraged Hungarians to demand reform and freedom.
significance: It showed that Moscow would use force to keep its bloc together.

title: Ghana becomes independent
